newsitem.title: USA: SGS-Thomson develops anti-pirate DVD chip.
newsitem.headline: SGS-Thomson develops anti-pirate DVD chip.

text.p: Europe's SGS-Thomson Microelectronics said Monday it developed an integrated circuit that protects digital video systems from copyright pirates who copy films, music and other material.
The company said it developed the anti-copy system, called Macrovision 7.0, with Macrovision Corp.

"Our product alleviates the concerns of copyright owners," SGS-Thomson said in a statement released here. "The chip is available in time for the development of DVD (digital video disc) products, which will be introduced this year."
The stock was trading up 3-1/8 at 43 by 1236 EDT/1636 GMT.

DVD players allow consumers to view movies on CD-sized disks. Many Hollywood movie studios were concerned the high-quality images would encourage pirates and asked DVD manufacturer to add an effective copy protection system.
The anti-copy system modifies the video signal so it can be viewed on a television but not recorded clearly on a VCR.

The company said Twenty-seven consumer electronics companies worldwide have already been licensed to use the technology embodied in the STV0117A, which meets the Macrovision revision 7.0 anticopy process. It said One leading DVD manufacturer has already chosen the part for a DVD player starting up mass production in the current quarter.
Macrovision Corp develops and markets technologies that protect video, audio, and data in both prerecorded and electronically transmitted formats from unauthorized viewing and unauthorized recording.
